title: Quarterly application access attestation missed its deadline
description: Synthetic scenario 001. An application owner did not finish the scheduled account recertification by quarter close. Sign-off was missing for several sampled accounts, leaving continued business need unconfirmed. Scope was limited to the fictional synthetic-client-a engagement sample.
remediation: Assign the review to a named process owner, complete a look-back of affected accounts, and add a deadline alert to the quarterly attestation tracker.
outcome: The owner reviewed the outstanding accounts; the next quarterly cycle completed on schedule with dated sign-offs.

title: Evidence gap: former staff account disablement was not traceable
description: Synthetic scenario 002. For a few departed workers, the audit could not establish when system access was shut off because the HR-to-identity handoff record was missing. Scope was limited to the fictional synthetic-client-a engagement sample.
remediation: Confirm the current status of sampled accounts, retain identity-system logs, and reconcile departure notices to disablement timestamps.
outcome: Most sampled accounts were shown disabled in system logs; an account without confirmation was escalated and shut down.

title: Review noted provisioning preceded manager authorization
description: Synthetic scenario 003. Some sampled access requests showed that a manager's sign-off occurred after the account change. The review found no evidence that the access was unauthorized. Scope was limited to the fictional synthetic-client-a engagement sample.
remediation: Reinforce the approval-before-access step and produce a timestamp exception listing for the access owner to review.
outcome: The approval sequence was corrected, and a later sample showed authorization recorded before provisioning.

title: Production deployment had no recorded pre-approval
description: Synthetic scenario 004. One sampled production release lacked an approval record from before implementation. A follow-up review found no identified adverse effect. Scope was limited to the fictional synthetic-client-a engagement sample.
remediation: Make pre-release approval a required workflow entry and have the change owner review emergency exceptions each month.
outcome: Workflow checks were added, and the next monthly sample contained complete approvals.

title: Evidence gap: one operator developed and released a production change
description: Synthetic scenario 005. A sampled release listed the same operator as developer and production deployer. The file contained no evidence of a separate post-release review. Scope was limited to the fictional synthetic-client-a engagement sample.
remediation: Separate release permissions, retrospectively inspect affected deployments, and alert when conflicting operator accounts are detected.
outcome: Conflicting permissions were removed and release monitoring was put in place.

title: Review noted aged reconciliation items lacked follow-up
description: Synthetic scenario 006. The monthly close included old reconciling items without a recorded escalation path or target resolution date. Scope was limited to the fictional synthetic-client-b engagement sample.
remediation: Define aging triggers, assign accountable roles to open items, and track each exception through documented resolution.
outcome: Owners were assigned to the aged items, and the next two close cycles showed timely escalation.
